name: Panch Mishali Chorchori
subtitle: five vegetables cooked dry in their own steam with panch phoron and ground mustard

ingredients.note: soaked, then ground to a paste

ingredients.qty: 3, one for the mustard paste and two slit
4 tbsp, added a spoon at a time

prepNotes: Soak the mustard seeds for 20 minutes in warm water with one green chilli and a pinch of salt, then grind to a fine paste with a little of that water. Ground dry, or ground too long, mustard turns bitter.
Cut every vegetable to roughly the same 5cm baton so they finish together. The radish and potato go in first because they are the slowest.
Chorchori is a dry dish cooked in the vegetables' own moisture. Keep a small cup of water beside the pan and add it a spoon at a time, only when the pan catches.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a wide kadhai until it smokes, then rest it off the heat for 30 seconds.
Add the panch phoron and dried chillies and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
steps.tip: A wide pan matters here. Crowded vegetables steam grey instead of catching colour.

steps.text: Add the potato and radish batons with the turmeric and salt and stir-fry uncovered for 5 minutes.
Add the pumpkin, beans and eggplant with the slit green chillies, toss well, then cover and cook on low for 10 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not stir more than twice or the batons break down into mush.

steps.text: Uncover and check: the vegetables should be nearly tender and the pan almost dry. Add a spoon of water only if it is sticking.
Stir in the mustard paste, chilli powder and sugar, and cook uncovered for 5 minutes so the raw mustard cooks off.
steps.tip: Keep the heat low once the mustard is in; boiled hard, it goes bitter.

steps.text: Raise the heat for a final 2 to 3 minutes to let the edges of the vegetables catch and brown a little.
Take off the heat, spoon over the last teaspoon of raw mustard oil if you like it sharp, and serve with rice and dal.

storage: Best eaten the day it is made, but it keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat uncovered in a pan so it stays dry rather than watery.
